good: The project collects facts, research, notes or records you want to rely on later.
costs: More structure: every fact needs a source and a date, so writing things down takes a little longer.
does: Keeps facts, research and notes in organized files, each with its source and date.
outcome: Answers come from your own recorded facts, and nothing has to be researched twice.
title: Knowledge and context
for: Projects whose job is to know things and answer from them: research, planning, records, notes, guides, decisions, a subject the user keeps coming back to.
notFor: Building software. A project that is mainly an application takes the app pack (it can take both if it also keeps a knowledge base).
menu: | K3 | Ingest files | ingest.md | process every file in inbox/: preserve originals in sources/, extract the facts into docs/knowledge, update the source register |
| K4 | Make a deliverable | deliverable.md | produce this as a new file in outputs/, built from the knowledge base, checked against the brief |
precedence: Files given with a question → `ingest.md` first (so the facts are recorded), then the research skill (section A from the project, C for anything new).
Answering, looking up or checking facts → the research skill: A when the knowledge base has it and it is current, C when it is missing, stale or the user wants current information.
layout: What the project knows, one topic per file
Every source, with date and reliability
Drop zone for the user's new files
Never edited, moved or deleted (hook: protect-originals)
A new version is a new file (hook: no-overwrite)
Working data the project keeps current (price lists, counts, tables the user edits)
Edited freely; its origin is noted in docs/knowledge/SOURCES.md

requirements.message: Research skill, section E: record the confirmed findings in docs/knowledge (labeled, sourced, dated) so the next question is answered from the project, not re-researched.

Answer from what the project knows: cite the knowledge files the answer came from by number, with a Sources: line for each ([1] docs/knowledge/...; web sources are fine for what the project doesn't have), or say plainly that the project has nothing recorded on it.
Register every ingested file in docs/knowledge/SOURCES.md (and move the originals into sources/).
Save the deliverable as a new file in outputs/ (a new version is a new file) and give its path.
Add a dated line to docs/CHANGELOG.md for the knowledge or outputs that changed.
Knowledge-capture skill: write the fact, preference or decision into docs/knowledge (labeled, sourced, dated), docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/BRIEF.md. Saying it in the answer is not recording it.
New originals arrived in sources/: follow the ingest runbook, so each one is registered in docs/knowledge/SOURCES.md and its facts are captured.
A file was written to outputs/: that is a deliverable, so follow the deliverable runbook (new version as a new file, sources, the writing check).

Facts were written into docs/knowledge: they come through the research skill (sources read this turn, cited), the knowledge-capture skill (what the user said) or the ingest runbook (a file they gave).
